_meta.description: Media ownership database. Every entry carries verify links — this file states what is publicly documented and points at the receipts. Figures are approximate and dated; ownership changes, so treat 'as_of' seriously and prefer the verify links for anything load-bearing.

foxnews.com.notes: Paid $787.5M to settle Dominion defamation suit (2023) over knowingly false election claims; internal messages showed hosts disbelieved on-air narratives.

nypost.com.notes: Same controlling family as Fox News and WSJ.

wsj.com.notes: News pages generally well-regarded; editorial page shares the owner's politics.

washingtonpost.com.notes: Owner intervened to block a presidential endorsement (2024) and redirected the opinion section (2025). Amazon holds major federal contracts.

latimes.com.notes: Owner blocked a presidential endorsement (2024); has pharma-industry holdings.

cnn.com.notes: Corporate parent carries heavy debt load; programming decisions have tracked ownership changes.

nbcnews.com.notes: Comcast is one of the largest US lobbying spenders and a major ISP with direct regulatory interests.

msnbc.com.notes: Spun off from Comcast with other cable properties in 2025; verify current structure.

abcnews.go.com.notes: Paid $15M to settle a Trump defamation suit (2024), a settlement widely criticized as capitulation with regulatory business pending.

cbsnews.com.notes: Paramount settled a Trump lawsuit over a routine '60 Minutes' edit (2025) while its merger needed federal approval.

owners: New York Times Co. (dual-class; Ochs-Sulzberger family control)

bloomberg.com.notes: Openly declined to investigate its owner during his presidential run.

owners: Nonprofit cooperative owned by member outlets
Nonprofit; member stations + sponsorship + (cut) federal funding
npr.org.notes: Federal funding rescinded in 2025; now more dependent on private sponsorship.

usatoday.com.notes: Largest US newspaper chain; deep newsroom cuts after SoftBank-backed merger.

chicagotribune.com.notes: Alden is known for acquiring newspapers and cutting staff far beyond industry norms.

denverpost.com.notes: Own editorial board publicly protested Alden's cuts ('news matters' revolt, 2018).

sinclairbroadcast.com.outlet: Sinclair Broadcast Group (185+ local TV stations)
sinclairbroadcast.com.notes: Forced local anchors nationwide to read identical 'must-run' political scripts (2018). If your local news is a Sinclair station, some segments are corporate-mandated.

owners: Axel Springer SE (KKR is largest shareholder)

newsmax.com.notes: Paid $40M to settle Smartmatic defamation suit (2024) and settled with Dominion (2025) over false election claims.

oann.com.notes: Court filings in defamation suits showed fabricated election-fraud programming; dropped by every major carrier.

dailywire.com.notes: Early funding from fracking billionaires Farris and Dan Wilks.

owners: Private — funders undisclosed by design (reporting has identified shipping-supply billionaire Dick Uihlein as a backer)
thefederalist.com.notes: Refuses to disclose funders; that refusal is itself information.

owners: Private (co-founded by Tucker Carlson; early funding from Foster Friess)
dailycaller.com.notes: Affiliated Daily Caller News Foundation is a 501(c)(3) taking foundation money — check its 990s.

theepochtimes.com.notes: CFO convicted in a $67M money-laundering scheme (2024–25 proceedings). Massive spender on pro-Trump social ads (2019–20).

townhall.com.outlet: Townhall (+ RedState, PJ Media, Hot Air, Twitchy)
townhall.com.notes: Salem is a Christian-conservative radio conglomerate; its web brands run as one editorial bloc.

washingtontimes.com.notes: Founded and sustained for decades at a loss by the Unification Church.

owners: Trump Media & Technology Group (majority: Donald Trump)
truthsocial.com.notes: A platform owned by a sitting politician is a campaign asset with a feed algorithm.

owners: Rumble Inc. (Chris Pavlovski; early investment from Peter Thiel and JD Vance)

x.com.notes: Owner is simultaneously a major government contractor, political donor, and the platform's loudest account; algorithmic reach and moderation have repeatedly shifted with his politics.

owners: Meta Platforms (Mark Zuckerberg, controlling voting shares)
facebook.com.notes: Ended US third-party fact-checking program (2025); engagement-ranked feeds structurally favor outrage.

youtube.com.notes: Recommendation engine optimizes watch time; radicalization-spiral dynamics are extensively documented.

forbes.com.notes: Most 'Forbes contributors' are unpaid/self-published — a byline there is not vetting.

owners: Substack Inc. (VC-backed: a16z led Series B)
substack.com.notes: Platform, not publisher: credibility is per-author, not per-domain.
